candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of floating solids or visible foam in other than trace amounts.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a qualitative enforceable discharge limit rather than a numeric one; interpreting 'trace amounts' differently could change whether an observation is classified as an exceedance, treated as non-numeric compliance, or left unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on the water, or coatings on stream banks.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes qualitative enforceable limits on oil, grease, and solids; different readings of 'visible' or what constitutes a prohibited discharge could change exceedance determinations or whether a numeric comparison is applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Samples taken in compliance with the monitoring requirements specified above shall be taken at the discharge from the final treatment unit prior to the receiving stream.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the required sampling location for monitoring tied to limits above; interpreting which upstream 'monitoring requirements' bind, or whether a reported sample was taken at the mandated point, could change which limits apply to a measurement and whether monitoring obligations were met.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall achieve compliance with the Cyanide effluent limitations specified for discharges in accordance with the following schedule:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links cyanide effluent limits to a compliance schedule rather than immediate applicability; interpreting when those referenced limitations become enforceable during FY2025 could change which cyanide limits are in effect and whether associated monitoring or reporting is required.

candidates.exact_span: Achieve Final Effluent Limitations 12 months after permit effective date
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a phased compliance deadline keyed to permit effective date; different interpretations of that date or whether FY2025 falls before or after the deadline could change whether cyanide limits are enforceable and whether interim progress-reporting obligations remain active.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall submit a progress report to both EPA and NMED outlining the status of the activities (i.e., analyzers installation, Process Optimization Study, etc.) during the months of January, April, July, and October, of each year, until compliance is achieved as stated above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes recurring quarterly progress-reporting obligations conditioned on not yet having achieved cyanide compliance; interpreting 'until compliance is achieved' differently could change whether reporting was required during specific FY2025 months.

candidates.exact_span: No later than 14 calendar days following the date for compliance for Cyanide effluent limitations, the permittee shall submit a written notice of compliance or noncompliance.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a time-bound reporting obligation tied to the cyanide compliance date; interpreting the trigger date or whether the notice was due during FY2025 could change evaluated monitoring/reporting requirements.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall achieve compliance with the TDS net increase effluent concentration limit of 449 mg/L 3 years after the permit effective date.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a numeric TDS net-increase limit of 449 mg/L with a start date keyed to permit effective date; interpreting the effective date or whether FY2025 is within the three-year window could change whether this limit is applicable and whether related monitoring comparisons should be performed.

candidates.exact_span: Complete constructions and cease discharging                 November 2024
candidates.computation_change_reason: Schedules cessation of a discharge by November 2024; interpreting whether and when that discharge actually ceased could change discharge-dependent monitoring obligations and whether later periods should be classified as documented no-discharge rather than missing-evidence cases.
